statement: The function returns a result r, and r = true if and only if G is a tree. G is a tree means (1) G is connected: for every u and v with 0 <= u < n and 0 <= v < n there is a finite sequence of vertices v0,...,vk such that v0 = u, vk = v, and for each j with 0 <= j < k the unordered pair {v_j, v_{j+1}} is an edge of G; and (2) G is acyclic: there are no integer k >= 3 and distinct vertices w0,...,w_{k-1} in {0,...,n-1} such that {w_j, w_{(j+1) mod k}} is an edge of G for every j with 0 <= j < k. Equivalently under the preconditions, r = true if and only if G is connected and len(edges) = n - 1 (with n read as its integer value).
preconditions: Let G be the simple undirected graph with vertex set {0,1,...,n-1} and edge set { {edges[i][0], edges[i][1]} | 0 <= i < len(edges) }. Assume 1 <= n <= 2000; 0 <= len(edges) <= 5000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(edges), len(edges[i]) = 2, 0 <= edges[i][0] < n, 0 <= edges[i][1] < n, and edges[i][0] != edges[i][1]; and for all i,j with 0 <= i < j < len(edges), the unordered pairs {edges[i][0], edges[i][1]} and {edges[j][0], edges[j][1]} are distinct.
